notes.meaning: Paul introduces himself as an apostle chosen by the will of God, not by human choice, and includes Timothy as his trusted brother in the faith. He writes to the believers in the city of Colossae, calling them holy people and faithful family members in Christ. He greets them with grace, which is God's free favor, and peace from God our Father.

Paul and Timothy continually thank God whenever they pray for the Colossian church. They are filled with gratitude because they have heard about the believers' firm trust in Jesus Christ. That faith shows itself in genuine love for all of God's holy people.

Their faith and love grow out of the secure hope kept safe for them in heaven. They first learned about this wonderful future when the true message of the gospel was preached to them. This good news is spreading across the Roman world and bearing fruit by changing lives, just as it did among them from the day they truly understood God's grace.

The Colossians had learned the good news from Epaphras, a dear coworker who faithfully served Christ on their behalf. Epaphras visited Paul in prison and brought an encouraging report about the church. He told Paul about the deep love that the Holy Spirit had created in their hearts.

Paul continually prays that God will give these believers deep spiritual wisdom to understand His will. Knowing what God wants helps them live lives that honor and please the Lord in every way. A life that pleases Christ produces good works like fruit on a tree and steadily grows closer to God.

Paul asks God to strengthen them with His own glorious power so they can endure hard times with patience and joy. Believers can gladly thank the Father, who has made them fit to share in the heavenly inheritance promised to His people. We do not earn this gift by our own good deeds, but receive it because God has prepared us for His kingdom of light.

God has rescued believers from the cruel power of spiritual darkness and brought them into the kingdom of His dearly loved Son. In Jesus we have redemption, which means being bought back from the slavery of sin. Through His sacrifice, all of our sins are freely and completely forgiven.

Jesus is the visible likeness of the invisible God, showing us clearly what God is like. Calling Him the firstborn over all creation does not mean He was created, but that He holds the highest rank, honor, and authority over everything made. He existed before any creature came into being and rules as supreme heir over all creation.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many modern scholars understand verses 15 through 20 to be an early Christian hymn about Christ that Paul quoted and applied to the Colossian church.

notes.meaning: Jesus created the entire universe, including earthly things and unseen spiritual powers like rulers and angels. Everything was made through His power and for His honor, showing that He is far above any angelic spirit. He existed before anything was made, and His power continually holds the whole universe together in order and balance.

Jesus is the head and leader of the church, which is described as His spiritual body. He is also the firstborn from the dead, being the first to rise with an immortal body that can never die. Because of His resurrection, He holds the first and highest place in all things.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic teaching holds that, under Christ, the Pope serves as a visible "ministerial" head of the church on earth.

notes.meaning: God was pleased to have all of His divine nature, power, and glory live permanently in Jesus Christ. Through Christ's death on the cross, God brought peace and reconciled a broken universe to Himself. To reconcile means to end hostility and restore a broken relationship to peace.

The Colossians were once separated from God, thinking of Him as an enemy and living in evil ways. But now God has brought them into friendship with Himself through the physical death of Jesus on the cross. Christ died so that He could present believers holy, pure, and without a single fault in God's presence.

differ.view: God fills believers with His Spirit and love so they can be made holy and blameless in this life, ready for the judgment.
This holiness is only begun now and grows daily. It is made complete only when Christ returns.

notes.meaning: Believers will stand blameless before God as they remain steadfast in their faith, resting on Christ like a building on a rock. Paul urges them not to be pushed away from the hope of the gospel, which was being preached widely throughout the Roman world. He reminds them that he was appointed as a servant to spread this very message.

differ.view: Methodists teach that this condition shows believers can lose the blessings of salvation if they fail to persevere in faith.
Reformed Christians believe that true believers will certainly persevere to the end, and this warning serves to keep them grounded and faithful.

notes.meaning: Paul rejoices in the hardships he faces while sharing the gospel with the Gentile world. His words about filling up what is lacking in Christ's sufferings do not mean that Christ's sacrifice on the cross was incomplete or needed human help. Instead, because Christ and the church are one body, Christ continues to feel and share in the afflictions of His people as they suffer for His sake.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic teaching has linked this verse to the idea that the sufferings of the saints, joined with Christ's, form a "treasury" the church can draw on when granting indulgences, which are releases from punishment due for sin.

notes.meaning: Paul became a servant of the church by the sacred duty and trust God gave him. God gave him this mission so that he could fully preach the message of salvation, especially to Gentiles who had never heard it before.

In the Bible, a mystery means a truth once kept hidden in God's plan but now openly revealed to His people. God chose to reveal this wonderful secret to Gentiles as well as Jews. The heart of this glorious truth is that Christ lives within believers, giving them the confident hope of sharing in God's eternal glory.

Paul and his companions preach Jesus Christ to everyone, warning them about sin and teaching God's truth with wisdom. Their goal is to help every believer reach full spiritual maturity in Christ. Paul works hard and strains like an athlete to achieve this, relying on the mighty power of Christ actively working inside him.
